title: Frozen interface identities churn on transitive dependency moves

minimal_reproducer.command: mncs abi native/mncs/debug/debug.mncs (before vs after the stdlib extraction)

expected_semantics: A module interface identity covers the module's own interface, so moving an unchanged dependency to a new repository does not invalidate every downstream frozen binding.
actual_behavior_limitation: The mncs.debug interface identity changed (7018beae to 31f110be) with zero source edits when stdlib files moved, failing closed every frozen host binding and native-application descriptor and taking the native debug core offline until regeneration.
why_capability_matters: Transitive coupling makes every dependency move a family-wide outage for frozen consumers; fail-closed is correct but the blast radius is large and silent until first use.
current_workaround: The mncs.remediation/1 provider detects stale identities and re-freezes them when the module source is git-clean; descriptors and bindings were regenerated for the extraction.

host_language_code_required.why: Detection and regeneration orchestration is host-side; identity semantics stay compiler-owned.

proposed_primitive_or_semantic_direction: Document whether transitive coupling is intended; if it is, publish a machine-readable identity-refresh procedure per consumer kind, or scope identities to the module interface plus declared dependency pins.
alternatives_considered: family-wide regeneration lockstep (manual, as done here)
tests_evidence: binding regeneration 7018beae to 31f110be with identical module source
resolution_criteria: Identity stability semantics are documented, and dependency moves either preserve consumer bindings or trigger a mechanical, detectable refresh.
